subject: Evaluation MAP: safeguarding burst charges and ramp caps
messages:

To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com; marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft MAP + quick Q on burst/overage protections

Hi Lauren / Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough today — the MAP draft attached was helpful. Before the execs sign off on timelines, procurement wants a clearer picture on how Redwood handles burst/overage during the evaluation and early ramp. A few concrete asks:

- Can we cap spend during the evaluation so we don't get surprise overage bills?
- What is the overage rate / rate card that would apply if we exceed the commit during ramp?
- Is there a way to reserve a small burst buffer (short-term) without committing to extra annual spend?

We're trying to align MAP milestones to procurement sign-offs: evaluation completion (~2-3 weeks), pilot ramp (30 days), production launch (target end of June). Attached is the MAP draft for reference.

Attaching: Acme_MAP_Draft.pdf (MAP draft)

For legal/procurement: looping in procurement@acmehealth.com and Jon Rogers (legal).

Appreciate a short note on guardrails and a proposed addendum we can hand to procurement.

Best,
Emma

Acme Health

Emma —

Thanks for the clear asks and the MAP draft. Short answers up-front, followed by a proposal you can share with procurement/legal:

1) Evaluation spend cap: yes — we can set a hard evaluation cap (hard stop) on the account during the MAP period. We typically set that at $X (you can pick the dollar limit) and enable billing alerts at 50% and 80%.

2) Overage / burst: We offer two mechanisms during ramp:
   - Soft burst: automatic temporary capacity increase up to Nx baseline for up to 72 hours. Overage billed at the posted burst rate on the rate card.
   - Hard cap: customer can opt to block requests once a hard spend or token cap is reached (no additional charges).

3) Reserve buffer: we can provision a small, reserved burst bucket (pre-purchased) that only applies during evaluation/pilot and is consumed before overage rates kick in. This gives predictable headroom without expanding the annual commit.

Attached is a short one-pager that outlines the guardrails and a sample clause procurement can add to the SOW:

- SoftBurst: 2x baseline for up to 72 hours per month, billed at $0.00045 per token over committed rate (example).
- Pre-purchased buffer: one-time $5,000 buffer applied during pilot; unused buffer rolls into month 1 of committed usage.
- Hard evaluation cap: account-level hard stop option enabled on request.

Please note the numbers above are placeholders; I'll loop in engineering for the recommended default values based on your eval profile.

Attachment: ramp-protections.pdf

Next step: if procurement is comfortable with a small buffer + hard cap, we can reflect that as an appendix to the MAP and push to legal for a redline. Happy to jump on a 30-min call tomorrow with Jon.

—Lauren

Subject: Re: Draft MAP + quick Q on burst/overage protections

Adding a technical perspective so procurement has clarity on how burst behavior maps to cost:

- Baseline and burst model: baseline = provisioned throughput (tokens/sec) tied to committed capacity. SoftBurst multiplies available throughput by a factor (e.g., 2x) for short durations. During SoftBurst we still meter actual tokens generated and bill per-token at the burst rate.

- KV/prefix caching: recommend enabling prefix caching for your evaluation workloads — common patient query patterns will see 20–40% token reduction on average in pilot benchmarks. This materially reduces burst exposure.

- Auto-pause and throttling: we can enable an auto-throttle rule that slows non-critical inference routes (batch jobs) if a spend threshold is breached during evaluation.

- Suggested initial numbers for Acme profile (based on our trial telemetry):
   * Suggested commit for pilot month: 500k tokens/day (30-day look)
   * SoftBurst allowance: up to 2x baseline for 72 hours once during the pilot window
   * Recommended pre-purchased buffer: $5k (consumes at burst rate before overage)

I've attached the latest public rate card for reference. Exact per-token rates are negotiable depending on commit and MAP milestones.

Attachment: ratecard-v3.xlsx

—Dev

Thanks — this is useful. A couple of follow-ups from procurement:

- Overages: Procurement is uncomfortable with a high per-token burst rate as it exposes Acme to variable spend. They're asking if Redwood can consider a capped overage rate for the pilot (e.g., no more than 1.5x standard committed rate) or a blended cap for the first 90 days.

- Buffer size: Can we make the $5k pre-purchased buffer smaller (e.g., $2k) if we agree to a small committed volume for the pilot month?

- MAP milestones & discounts: Procurement would like the MAP to include a milestone discount: once the pilot achieves the 'safety' metrics (latency < 200ms p95, inference success > 99%) and a handoff to infra is complete, we'd get an X% reduction applied to the first year commit. Is that something you can commit to in writing?

Looping in Jon for legal terms — Jon, please advise if we need a short SOW appendix for the buffer/overage language.

Appreciate a revised SOW appendix that we can circulate. Also proposing a call Wed morning to finalize numbers.

Best,
Emma

Emma / Jon / procurement —

Thanks — appreciate the clear signal on what procurement needs. We can absolutely tighten this up. Proposed appendix language and commercial levers below (I included concrete numbers to speed legal review):

1) Pilot buffer & cap
   - Pre-purchased buffer: $2,000 (applies first, consumed at pilot burst rate).
   - Hard evaluation cap: Acme may enable an account-level hard stop at $7,500 for the evaluation window.

2) Overage / burst pricing
   - Blended capped overage cap for first 90 days: no more than 1.5x the committed token rate.
   - SoftBurst behavior: up to 2x baseline for up to 72 hours; burst tokens billed at capped blended rate during the 90-day window.

3) MAP milestone discounts (apply to year-1 commit)
   - Milestone A (Pilot acceptance): 7% discount on committed unit price.
   - Milestone B (Production live on Dedicated): additional 5% (stacking) and $10k service credit applied to month 1.

4) Telemetry & controls
   - Billing alerts at 50/80/95% thresholds; automatic pause for non-critical routes if 95% is breached (enabled by default).

5) Next steps / docs
   - I've prepared a short SOW appendix with the above language and a redline ready for legal; attaching redline-sow.docx.
   - Proposed next step: 30-min procurement + legal call Wed 09:00 PT to finalize numbers and sign off on appendix.

If that captures what you need, I'll kick this to legal and create a HubSpot task to track the MAP milestones against the deal.

Thanks,
